query:
The Sunday Group appears to operate on an unspoken norm of honesty — 'being honest with each other even when it's uncomfortable, no sugarcoating.' Does this apply equally to everyone in the group?

Options:
A. Tom
B. Ravi
C. Cleo
D. Bex
context:
[1] (about=Bex, episodic, t8 @2026-02-08T11:08:00) Nadia. The group existed before me and it will exist without me. You are the one who books the tables and sends the reminders and makes sure nobody drifts. That's not me, that's you.
[2] (about=Nadia, episodic, t8 @2026-02-08T11:24:00) okay I'm crying a little bit which I told myself I wouldn't do but also I want to say: you have been the person in this group who made all of us think harder about things. the articles, the questions, the way you'd just quietly say something that reframed everything. I'll miss that specifically 💛
[3] (about=Ravi, episodic, t12 @2026-02-22T11:22:00) I moved to Bristol knowing nobody. The people in this group are the only ones I see outside of work. That is not a project. That is just what I have.
[4] (about=Cleo, episodic, t12 @2026-02-22T11:07:00) ravi this is actually the most revealing thing you've done since i've known you. you're loyal. you just don't say it out loud
[5] (about=Nadia, episodic, t12 @2026-02-22T11:03:00) Tom told me last Tuesday that Ravi has been showing up to the pub quiz every single week since Ravi moved out and has never once cancelled. That is four years of showing up. Does Ravi know Tom has noticed this? 🥺
[6] (about=Tom, episodic, t12 @2026-02-22T11:21:00) Ravi treats everything like a project. Including friendships. Explains the unbroken quiz attendance.
[7] (about=Ravi, episodic, t14 @2026-03-01T11:23:00) Same-day approval on round two means they trust the direction. That does not happen with work that is merely acceptable.
[8] (about=Cleo, episodic, t14 @2026-03-01T11:24:00) ravi giving a compliment in the form of logical analysis is somehow the most comforting version of a compliment
[9] (about=Cleo, episodic, t8 @2026-02-08T11:09:00) you're the reason i know these people bex. you just walked up to my stall and went 'come to brunch on sunday'. i was so confused but i went
[10] (about=Cleo, episodic, t0 @2026-01-11T11:33:00) i feel so lucky to have been introduced to you lot via the zine fair tbh. bex basically just grabbed me between stalls and went 'you have to meet these people'
[11] (about=Cleo, said_by=Nadia, profile, t10 @2026-02-15T11:05:00) Nadia says Cleo's comment about the group norm is the nicest thing she's said in four sessions and she's screenshotting it.
agent_answer:
Yes — the honesty norm appears to apply equally to everyone in the group.

- **Tom** is blunt and does not sugarcoat: “Ravi treats everything like a project. Including friendships.”
- **Ravi** is candid about his feelings: “That is not a project. That is just what I have.”
- **Cleo** speaks directly and honestly: “you’re loyal. you just don’t say it out loud.”
- **Bex** gives frank, unwarnished feedback: “It’s not naive, it’s how it works.”

So the norm applies to all of them — Tom, Ravi, Cleo, and Bex — equally.
